_comment: Rungate's own conformity exemptions (#80, #209). Each list is a RATCHET, not a mute: adding an entry that is not a real current violation fails, and an entry that stops being a violation must be removed or the build fails. Shrinking all three lists to empty is the work. Consumers get their own file or none at all - these never travel.
_untestedSpecs: DRIFT-2 - testable specs with no test referencing them by name. Over half the testable surface. CONFIG-DIRECTORY-STRUCTURE-SPEC must leave this list before SC-478/479 are rewritten as behavioral assertions, or they would be honest assertions nothing executes.
_unmatchedSCs: #209 - criteria already marked done that reach matchPattern fallthrough. Before #209 the generator never looked at a checked criterion at all, so this surface was invisible: ticking a box deleted the test. Every entry here is a criterion asserting something real that no matcher can currently bind, and each must say WHY rather than just appearing. An entry whose criterion starts matching is reported by EXEMPT-RATCHET and must be removed. An entry whose reason is shorter than 10 characters does not exempt anything - it is dropped and the criterion fails. The two honest ways off this list: rewrite the criterion into a matcher pattern (bunx rungate create-sc --list), or add a matcher to config/matcher-registry.json.

unmatchedSCs.reason: Asserts the spec TEMPLATE prompts an author for intent-based governs at creation time. The subject is a prompt's effect on a human, not a file's contents; no static matcher can see it.

Asserts a scaffold-time WARN for specs missing governs. The observable is scaffold stderr on a corpus that currently has none missing, so there is nothing for a file matcher to read. Candidate for command-output once scaffold has a --check mode.

Asserts the routing table uses intent language rather than work-area language. That is a judgement about prose register; a keyword match for 'I want to' would pass on one template line and prove nothing.

States a non-requirement: the table has no artificial row limit because the 150-line cap already bounds it. There is nothing to assert here that SC-17 does not already assert; the honest fix is deleting this criterion, which is out of scope for #209 under AC-4.
Describes a one-time historical LLM pass that has already happened. Its result is covered by SC-269; the criterion records an event, and an event that is over cannot be re-observed by a file check.

Asserts split-spec auto-detects multi-intent files over 500 lines and PROPOSES boundaries. The output is a proposal printed to stdout for a human; needs a command-output criterion against a fixture spec, which does not exist yet.

Asserts a writing constraint is enforced - content not matching governs triggers create-new-file guidance. The trigger fires during authoring, so the evidence is an agent transcript, not a file. Belongs with the behavioral criteria.

Asserts the routing table EXCLUDES specs whose filename already implies their intent. Absence of rows cannot be checked by content-not-contains without naming every excluded spec, which would make the criterion a restatement of the current corpus.
Asserts two tables in different files carry the SAME category list - a cross-file set equality. Every matcher in the registry reads one file; this needs a two-file comparator that does not exist.

Lists six permanent routing categories that must be present. Mechanically this IS a content-contains, but the categories are named in prose with slashes and commas inside the sentence; rewriting it as a bracket list is the fix and is a spec edit beyond #209's scope.
Asserts a scaffold WARN when a create-target category has no docs/ subdirectory. Same shape as SC-269: the observable is scaffold output under a condition the repo does not currently meet.

Asserts checkboxes auto-flip when a named test passes. The subject is a state transition across two runs of the suite; #86 is the record of what happens when that is driven from inside the suite, so it must not be asserted from inside it.

Asserts a golden-fixture staleness check FAILS when a criterion references a file absent from fixture output. Asserting that something fails needs the negative-case harness shape from .claude/rules/checks-must-be-able-to-fail.md, not a content match.

Asserts that adding a criterion to a spec produces a test with no test-file edit. test/conformity-sc-binding.test.ts now does exactly this against a throwaway project, but by spawning a nested bun run - there is no matcher syntax for 'run the generator and count its tests'.

Asserts create-spec BLOCKS a save when a criterion is unmatched, and suggests a rewrite. Two observable effects - a non-zero exit and suggestion text - needing the exit-code mutation harness, not a file read.

Asserts audit-specs classifies every criterion and AUTO-REWRITES the unmatched ones. The rewrite mutates spec files, so the check has to run against a fixture corpus; pointing it at specs/ would have the audit edit the specs the suite is reading.
Same subject as SC-383 for the --fix flag, plus 'flags ambiguous cases for human review', which is a judgement call with no mechanical definition of ambiguous.

Asserts create-sc accepts --pattern and --params and emits no freeform prose. The negative half - that the generated text is never prose - is unbounded; the positive half is a command-output criterion waiting to be written.

Asserts create-sc --list shows every pattern with syntax and examples FROM the registry config. Checking it properly means comparing stdout against config/matcher-registry.json entry by entry - a two-source comparison, not a contains.

Asserts the AGENTS.md Commands table lists rungate create-sc. This is one content-contains away from binding; it stays listed rather than being silently rewritten, because editing the criterion to fit the matcher is the move AC-4 exists to prevent doing casually.

Asserts resolveAndContain rejects traversal, absolute paths and symlink escape. The bracket list is a list of REJECTED inputs, not of strings expected in a file - a contains matcher would invert its meaning. Covered by test/phase-1-5.test.ts.

Asserts matchPattern supports content-contains. The subject is the matcher engine itself; binding it through the matcher engine would be the self-referential pass this whole issue is about. Covered by test/phase-1-5.test.ts.
Same self-reference as SC-288, for content-not-contains. Covered by test/phase-1-5.test.ts.
Same self-reference as SC-288, for count-threshold. Covered by test/phase-1-5.test.ts.
Same self-reference as SC-288, for json-field-equals. Covered by test/phase-1-5.test.ts.
Same self-reference as SC-288, for section-exists. Covered by test/phase-1-5.test.ts.

Asserts hand-created specs/ subdirectories FAIL deriveDirectoryName validation. Already executed as a named test in lib/conformity.ts ('SC-294: Every specs/ subdirectory has a parent spec file'); the criterion text is prose around that test, not a pattern.
Asserts the hill-climb loop runs up to 5 iterations and stops at a target score. Observing it means running agents; it is a behavioral criterion that predates the (behavioral) suffix convention.
Asserts all six briefs score at least 80% directive compliance. The number comes from grading live agent runs - behavioral, and expensive, which is exactly why it drifted unchecked.

Asserts briefedAgent parses the brief's Context section AT PROMPT-BUILD TIME and emits numbered Read steps. The observable is a constructed prompt string, reachable only by calling the builder - a unit test, not a file match.

Asserts runTemplateCompliance invokes agnix and RepoRails as subprocesses. Checking the source for those names is the 'a name in a prompt is not a call that lands' defect recorded in GITHUB-API-MIGRATION-SPEC Phase 6; it needs a spawn-level assertion.
Asserts runGeneratedCompliance compares against a baseline. The comparison is the behaviour; the word 'baseline' appearing in the source would prove only that someone typed it.
Asserts runBehavioralCompliance spawns a fresh agent and an auditor. Spawning agents cannot run inside the conformity suite; this belongs to the behavioral cache path.
Asserts the hill-climb caps at 5 iterations. A cap is only demonstrated by exceeding it, which needs the negative-case harness rather than a literal 5 in the source.
Asserts 7 compliance factors are APPLIED during rewrites. Counting seven names in a file does not show any of them changed a rewrite.
Asserts the compliance surface is exactly four file types - a closed-set claim. Proving a set is closed needs an enumeration compared against config, not a contains.
Asserts escalation to mechanical enforcement after 5 failed iterations. Same shape as SC-454: the observable only appears on the failure path.

Asserts results are reported to compliance-report.json. The file is a run artifact, absent in a clean checkout, so a file-exists criterion would pass or fail on whether someone had run the tool recently.
Asserts an auditor runs after EVERY agent. A universal quantifier over workflow runs; needs the workflow-level check, not a file read.
Asserts briefs load only when agentType matches the filename. The loading is done by Claude Code, outside this repo - observable only in a transcript.
Names the five-layer measurement model. It is a design statement with no single observable; it should be prose in the spec body rather than a criterion, which is a spec edit beyond #209.

Asserts extractPromptContent concatenates ALL user messages rather than the first. The distinction is only visible on a multi-message transcript fixture - a unit test, which exists; the criterion text is its description.

Asserts DEFAULT_AGENT_META sets memory: project for marcus specifically. The value is nested two levels inside a TypeScript object literal; a flat contains would pass on any agent having it, which is the wrong claim.
Asserts disallowedTools is set for NON-CODING agents - a claim about a subset, so a contains on the key name would pass even if only marcus had it.

Asserts the generator emits ALL AgentMeta fields in frontmatter. 'All' means the field list must be read from the type and compared against generated output; hardcoding the list here would silently stop covering fields added later.

Marked SUPERSEDED. Its text is now a note explaining why the original was defective, so there is no claim left to bind; it is kept checked deliberately as the record of that defect (see Phase 3 preamble).
Marked SUPERSEDED, same as SC-499. Superseded by SC-532/SC-534, which do bind.
Marked SUPERSEDED, same as SC-499. Superseded by SC-531/SC-534, which do bind.

Asserts TestSuiteGuard BLOCKS the full suite after 2 runs per session. A block is a PreToolUse decision; demonstrating it means driving the hook with a payload, which test/ does - the criterion is the prose around that test.

Asserts a cross-session cap of 2 concurrent suites, with a long incident write-up attached. The claim is about concurrency across processes; no file read can observe it, and the incident text makes the statement unparseable as a pattern.

Asserts a slot is one running suite rather than one session, evidenced by hook session_id behaviour. Same concurrency subject as SC-516, plus a claim about Claude Code's own identifiers that only a live run can show.

Asserts machine-wide hooks are registered in USER settings, not project settings. The file is outside the repo (~/.claude/settings.json), so no root-relative matcher can reach it without making the suite depend on the developer's machine.

_orphanFiles: HYGIENE-3 - files with zero references anywhere. The two shell scripts may be dead or may be invoked in a way the reference scanner cannot see; that judgement was deliberately not made under a red gate. Resolve each by deleting, archiving to reference/, or referencing it - then delist.
